gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-old-hunga: Bloody storms in with fat, round lowercase bowls and a commanding, slightly menacing look, while Noto Sans Old Hungarian stays friendly beneath it. Big heading, modest body works nicely.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-old-itali: Bloody hits hard with big round bowls and a menacing, commanding streak. Noto Sans Old Italic does the opposite job, packing its lowercase close to the capitals in height with curve endings held well apart.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-old-north: Commanding is how the heading lands, with Bloody's big round lowercase bowls taking over the top of the page. And Noto Sans Old North Arabian would feel cramped and dense if pushed large, with its tall lowercase band and outward-pointing terminals.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-old-permi: Noto Sans Old Permic has rounded forms that stay clearly open to the side, and its lowercase nearly matches the capitals in height. Bloody, by contrast, is all menace, with big round bowls built to make a headline loud.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdi: Approachable is the body's first impression, thanks to a tall x-height that nearly reaches cap height under Bloody's big round bowls. Noto Sans Old Sogdian then keeps its wide-mouthed letters crisp, so the heading's menace never swamps the text.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-old-turki: Noto Sans Old Turkic brings chunky, tall lowercase letters with open-mouthed curves that stay clear, sitting under the round-bowled menace of Bloody. Its strongest quality is sheer friendliness.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Noto Sans Oriya keeps its curve gaps generous and its small letters almost as tall as the capitals, under Bloody's loud, round-bowled heading. Text stays easygoing throughout.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-osage: Noto Sans Osage fills the line with inflated lowercase bowls and sweeping curves that never close up, under the round-bowled snarl of Bloody. And that shared roundness, one shouting and one friendly, is what ties them.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Noto Sans Osmanya reads crisp and tidy, with wide, easy s turns. Its oversized lowercase looks sturdy beside the big round bowls of Bloody, which supplies all the drama up top.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hm: Loud, round and a little menacing, that is Bloody. Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong sits below with a high-set x-height and rounds that gap like a cracked bangle, giving the shouting heading something sturdy to lean on.
